title: Anthropic's AI wrote so much code Git could not keep up (Thu 12 Nov, redrawn 13 Nov)

explains.git: Git is the tool almost every programmer uses to save and share code (card 1)

cards.headline: Its AI wrote so much code, Git couldn't keep up
cards.line: Git is the tool almost every programmer uses to save and share code. Here's what broke it.
cards.picture: The cover as approved: a robot arm in a storm of paper over a filing cabinet

cards.headline: 12 times more code a day than in May.
cards.line: Code changes saved per day at Anthropic.
cards.picture: Two bars to scale: 2,500 in May, 30,000+ in September

cards.headline: Git became the traffic jam.
cards.line: The tool every programmer uses to save code was built for people, not for an AI flood.
cards.picture: Rows of code changes piling up at a narrow funnel marked GIT

cards.headline: So 7 engineers built a new Git for AI.
cards.line: 5 months. It's called Scion. Claude wrote most of its code. GitHub and others are building the same.
cards.picture: Seven figures, and the name Scion

cards.headline: Your next software: built for AI to use, people to check.
cards.line: Ask who your next tool was built for.
cards.picture: A robot handing to a person with a tick

read_back.reader: Fresh reader A (Haiku, a 12-year-old, headlines only, once)
read_back.retold: AI wrote so much computer code, about 12 times more in four months, that Git, the tool programmers use to save and share code, got jammed. So seven engineers built a new tool made for AI, and future software will be built so AI can use it and people can check it.

read_back.reader: Fresh reader B (Sonnet, a shop owner who never wrote code, headlines only, once)
read_back.retold: An AI company's tools wrote so much code, about 12 times more in four months, that the system programmers use to save and share code got overloaded and jammed. So seven engineers built a new one designed for AI, and the point for me is that future software will be made by AI and checked by people.

sources: Anthropic engineering, Redesigning source control, 13 Oct 2026 (2,500 to 30,000+ merges a day; Git its biggest bottleneck; seven engineers, five months, Scion)
